newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada minister won't re-regulate air transport.
newsitem.headline: Canada minister won't re-regulate air transport.

text.p: Canadian Transport Minister David Anderson on Monday ruled out any government re-regulation of the air transport industry as a step to saving financially troubled Canadian Airlines Corp.

In notes for a speech to the Air Transport Association of Canada, Anderson said labor leaders seeking a solution to Canadian Airlines' problems are proposing a return to federal regulation of domestic routes and also want the Canada-U.S. "Open Skies" agreement on cross-border traffic rescinded.

"My response is this: outlawing seat sales and shutting down discount carriers will not ultimately save a single job at Canadian," Anderson said. "Furthermore, turning back the clock would be contrary to the interests of the travelling public."

Anderson said a federal government bailout of Canadian Airlines cannot work as a substitute for serious restructuring. He said the federal government and two Canadian provinces provided Canadian Airlines with C$120 million in loan guarantees during the company's last restructuring.

"But more loan guarantees to cover more losses will do nothing to secure the future of this important enterprise. Similarily, there is no regulatory quick-fix preventing an airline from offering the competition and choice its customers want will not secure a prosperous future."
Anderson said Canadian Airlines has put forward a "realistic plan" to reverse its chronic losses and he thinks the plan will succeed.

Canadian Airlines' major unions are opposed to the carrier's request for an across-the-board employee wage rollback that would save the airline C$70 million a year. Canadian has said the 10-percent wage cut is crucial to the airlines' survival.
